newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rocket to 2nd straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rocket to 2nd straight record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose sharply in heavy trade Wednesday to notch up their second record close in as many sessions.
Traders said stocks rallied on sharp falls in primary interest rates, a favourable outlook for fourth quarter earnings reports and technical factors.
The leading IPC share index ended up 52.60 points, or 1.40 percent, at 3,802.63. Volume was exceptional at 215.1 million shares traded.
"Great market. Dealing was very heavy, foreigners bought massively on primary rate cuts and technical breakthroughs," a trader from the Vector brokerage said.
The central bank assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bill, rates at 19.69 percent at its weekly auction on Tuesday evening, a fall of 1.76 percentage points since last week.
Analysts said a favourable outlook for fourth quarter earnings reports also fuelled the rally.

"The market was obviously influenced by the sharp falls in interest rates and the pace set by foreign buyers, but the posting of fourth quarter reports is also playing an important part," said Daniel Romo, an analyst at the Bancrecer bank.
"There will have to be intraday profit-taking before the bourse climbs again at the end of the month," he added.
Technical analysts noted the bourse broke firm resistance at 3,750 points and was stable at 3,800, which they said gave stocks potential to rally towards the 3,900-point mark.
Traders also pointed to the record-breaking close on Wall Street as another catalyst for the bourse's performance.
"The Dow gained more than 100 points and that helped ADRs to haul up local shares," one trader said.
The Dow Jones rallied 103.52 points, or 1.51 percent, to 6,961.63 points.
Telmex ADRs gained 1-1/2 to 40-1/2 on Wall Street, while its L shares, which accounted for 11 percent of shares traded in Mexico, soared 58 centavos (7 cents) to 15.82 pesos ($2.03).
On the broad market, 124 stocks changed hands, of which 71 gained while 32 were down.
The most heavily traded gainer, after Telmex L shares, was financial stock GFB, which gained 18 centavos (2 cents) to 3.29 pesos (42 cents).
Traders said the stock recovered after being punished in recent weeks, adding the financial sector as a whole benefitted from recent falls in primary interest rates.
Dealers noted that decliners were traded at much smaller volumes than gainers, and did not much influence dealing during the session.
